newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Kuchma signs decree accepting PM's resignation.
newsitem.headline: Kuchma signs decree accepting PM's resignation.

text.p: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma signed a decree on Wednesday accepting his prime minister's resignation on health grounds, a spokeswoman for Kuchma said.

"The president has signed a decree accepting the resignation of Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko, who said he needed medical treatment. His resignation letter says he will be unable to fulfil his duties for two or three months," she said.

Deputies in parliament, who will have to approve Kuchma's candidate to replace Lazarenko, said leaders of parliamentary groups were expecting to meet the president for talks on the subject at 4 p.m. (1300 GMT).
Kuchma removed Lazarenko, 44, from his post temporarily on June 19 while he was ill, a move which was widely interpreted as a ploy and as meaning that Lazarenko was being sacked.

Some analysts believe Lazarenko initiated the move so he could depart from power with dignity as Kuchma cannot sack a minister who is sick. Others say Kuchma feared him as a powerful rival and hesitated to sack him outright.

The president named Lazarenko's deputy, Vasyl Durdynets, as acting prime minister on June 19. But parliament, which closes from mid-July to September, must approve his appointment within 60 days and several other candidates have been suggested since.
